sections.html: Labeo longipinnis from the Congo River was presented in Europe for the first time in December 2005. It grows to about 30 cm long and is not noticeable for a particularly spectacular design or colour.
Only roomy containers are suitable for keeping this fish.
A generous filtering unit should always be present with large bottom feeders.
Labeo place no increased requirements on nutrition, except as regards quantity.

Thanks to its lively manner, beautiful form and fins, it can become a genuine "eye-catcher" in the community aquarium. Since no references on its behaviour in aquaria exist so far, there is still a lot to discover. One should start with a not too small number of animals, since almost nothing is known about its social behaviour. Labeo species can become quite incompatible with age, and it is then always favourable when the aggression can be distributed within a group.
